characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Rigaku, D/Max-RB, Cu target, 40 kV, 150 mA
characterization_methods.key_findings: No κ-carbide reflections in specimens annealed at 900 °C and above (including 1200 °C); α lattice parameter 2.89–2.91 Å, γ lattice 3.65–3.67 Å, κ-carbide lattice 3.76–3.79 Å (for specimens with κ).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Zeiss AxioCam MRc5; specimens mechanically polished and etched with 8% Nital
characterization_methods.key_findings: Banded structure persists but becomes less contiguous and coarser at higher annealing temperatures (up to 900 °C series shown).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEI Quanta 450, acceleration voltage 20 kV; specimens etched with 8% Nital
characterization_methods.key_findings: At 1200 °C, banded structure with coarse α and γ grains (Fig. 6(h)); dense needle- and plate-shaped FCC particles in some large α grains and bright boundary κ-carbide film (Fig. 10(d)).
characterization_methods.purpose: Microstructure observation and grain-size measurement (with ImageJ)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEOL 2100, acceleration voltage 200 kV; thin foils twin-jet polished in 10% perchloric acid + 90% alcohol at −30 °C, 30 V
characterization_methods.key_findings: TEM BF (Fig. 12(a)) shows a bright band-like boundary κ between two large α grains; SADP (Fig. 12(b)) shows the N–W orientation relationship between κ-carbide and α matrix; (200)κ DF (Fig. 12(c)) from [110]κ shows only part of the boundary κ-carbide.
characterization_methods.purpose: Examination of boundary phases, orientation relationships and dislocation substructure
characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) with selected-area diffraction (SAD)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: EDS attached to the FEI Quanta 450 SEM
characterization_methods.key_findings: κ-carbide is enriched in Mn and Al with Fe depletion relative to α and γ; used to confirm α (Al-rich), γ (Mn- and C-rich) and κ-carbide (Mn- and Al-rich).
characterization_methods.purpose: Examination of element concentrations in different phases

characterization_methods.key_findings: For 1200 °C: ultimate strength 611 MPa, yield strength 495 MPa, ultimate elongation 4.8%.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; initial strain rate 3 × 10^-4 s^-1; gage length 50 mm, gage width 12.5 mm; tensile axis parallel to the rolling direction
characterization_methods.purpose: Measurement of engineering/true stress–strain behaviour and tensile properties

characterization_methods.key_findings: Density about 6.80 g/cm³, about 13% lower than pure Fe.

analytical_models.equation_role: predicts equilibrium fractions of α, γ, κ and liquid versus temperature
analytical_models.model_note: Calculated κ vanishes (eutectoid γ → α + κ) at 823 °C; ferrite lowest fraction around 1000 °C.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Composition Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C (wt.%); fractions of equilibrium phases ferrite (α), austenite (γ) and κ-carbide (κ) computed for temperatures above 550 °C
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: General trend of phase fractions similar to XRD-measured values, but calculated κ-carbide dissolution (eutectoid) temperature 823 °C is lower than the measured 850–900 °C; differences attributed to non-equilibrium state of the steel and to calculated atomic fractions vs measured volume fractions.

defect_interactions.interaction_type: misorientation between neighbouring boundary κ-carbide particles
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: The (200)κ dark-field micrograph taken from the [110]κ direction shows only part of the boundary κ-carbide, indicating a large misorientation between the neighbouring κ-carbide particles (which are otherwise N–W related to α).

defect_interactions.interaction_type: quench-formed needle/plate-like FCC particles in α promote cracking
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: In the specimen annealed at 1200 °C the needle-like or plate-like particles in some large α grains will undoubtedly promote cracking.

interfaces.interface_notes: In the annealing temperature range 900–1200 °C, κ-carbide along α/α boundaries of large grains dissolves last (dissolution temperature of κ-carbide along α/α boundary is higher than that along α/γ boundary).
interfaces.phase_evolution: κ-carbide has dissolved during annealing at 1200 °C (dissolution temperature between 850 °C and 900 °C); the boundary κ-carbide observed in the 1200 °C specimen is believed to form during quenching, and needle/plate-like FCC particles form from a quick BCC→FCC transformation during quenching in some large α grains.

phase_interfaces.coherence: Nishiyama–Wasserman orientation relationship between κ-carbide and α matrix (z = [001]κ, [001]κ//[011]α, (110)α//(11-1)κ)

interfaces.slip_behavior: No obvious TRIP or TWIP phenomenon found during the tensile test according to TEM examination of the deformed microstructure; work-hardening rate of specimens annealed at or over 900 °C is lower than that of κ-carbide-bearing 700–850 °C specimens at true strain below about 5%.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: A 20 kg ingot of the Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C steel was prepared by vacuum induction melting.
The ingot was heated to 1200 °C and then forged.
processing_steps.reduction_ratio: forged to forging blank with cross section of about 40 mm × 60 mm

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Forging blank homogenized at 1200 °C for 1 h before hot rolling.
The forging blank was hot-rolled to a 3 mm plate with finishing rolling temperature around 880 °C.
processing_steps.reduction_ratio: hot-rolled to a plate of 3 mm thickness

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: After rolling the plate was water quenched to about 300 °C; the schematic in figure_001 shows water cooling to the 300 °C level then air cooling.
The hot-rolled plate was annealed at various temperatures from 700 °C to 1200 °C for 1 h; for this sample the annealing temperature is 1200 °C.
After annealing the specimen was water quenched; the boundary κ-carbide and the needle/plate-like FCC particles in large α grains are thought to form during quenching.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: tensile axis parallel to the rolling direction; specimens machined from the annealed and water-quenched plate; tested by a universal testing machine (CMT 4105)
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: gage length of 50 mm and gage width of 12.5 mm

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress–engineering strain curve (Fig. 15(a)) and true stress–true strain together with work hardening rate curves (Fig. 15(b)) for the 1200 °C, 1 h specimen; curve lies below those of lower annealing temperatures and continuous yielding (no yield phenomenon).

microstructure_list.region: overall annealed specimen (RD–ND section shown in Fig. 6(h); large α grains with FCC particles in Fig. 10(d))

structures.number_of_phases: 3 main phases (α, γ, κ-carbide), plus quench-formed needle/plate-like FCC particles in α
structures.overall_structure: Microstructure of the Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C steel annealed at 1200 °C for 1 h and water quenched, consisting mainly of ferrite (α), austenite (γ) and boundary κ-carbide; no matrix κ-carbide resolvable (κ-carbide dissolved above ~900 °C). The banded structure persists but becomes less contiguous at higher temperature (RD–ND section, Fig. 6(h)). Needle-shaped or plate-shaped FCC particles formed during quenching are present in some large α grains. α and γ grains are large and coarsened after annealing at 1200 °C.

unmapped_findings: Product of strength and ductility of the 1200 °C, 1 h specimen: 3 GPa% (Table 1); this is the lowest among the annealed specimens (700–1200 °C), for which the maximum was 31 GPa% at 900 °C.

The 1200 °C annealed specimen has the largest grains: α₂ (banded ferrite) = 68.4 μm and γ = 36.0 μm (Fig. 9); grain growth, rather than phase-fraction change, is the main reason for the decrease of strength and elongation above 900 °C.
The austenite (γ) volume fraction of the 1200 °C specimen is about 57%, within the narrow 57–63% range that γ occupies between 900 °C and 1200 °C (Fig. 14).
No matrix κ-carbide is detected by XRD in the 1200 °C specimen, but boundary κ-carbide (formed during quenching) exists in the specimen, as it does in all specimens annealed at or above 900 °C.
Yield phenomenon (associated with ferrite steels) only appears in the 700 °C specimen; the 1200 °C annealed specimen shows continuous yielding.

In the 1200 °C specimen the needle-like or plate-like FCC particles in some large α grains will undoubtedly promote cracking, and the ductile fracture area lessens with increasing annealing temperature up to 1200 °C.

The present steel's tensile property comparison (Table 2) lists the (900 °C) present-steel values [UTS 855 MPa, YS 651 MPa, γ+α(40%)+boundary κ, elongation 36.6%, product 31 GPa%] against literature Fe–Mn–Al–C steels; these are the optimum present-steel values, not the 1200 °C values.
